title: Sod Calculator: Pallets, Rolls and Cost
description: Work out how much sod you need in square feet, rolls and pallets, with a waste guide, a worked example and 2026 sod prices per square foot.

cover.alt: Illustration of a roll of sod on a outdoor & yard blueprint background with a measuring tape

keywords: how many pallets of sod do I need
how much sod do I need
takeaways: One pallet of sod covers about 450 sq ft, and one standard roll covers about 10 sq ft.

body:
A sod calculator turns lawn size into square feet, rolls and pallets, then prices the job. The short version: measure the lawn, add waste for cuts, divide by 450 sq ft per pallet, and round up. A 1,500 sq ft lawn with 10 percent waste needs 1,650 sq ft of sod, which is 4 pallets or 165 standard rolls. HomeGuide puts sod material at $0.30 to $0.80 per sq ft in 2026, so that lawn runs about $495 to $1,320 for sod alone. If the soil under the lawn is thin or low, fix it first with our [topsoil calculator](/blog/topsoil-calculator/).

## The formula

**Lawn area = length x width, added up for every section**

**Sod to order = lawn area x (1 + waste percent)**

**Pallets = sod to order / pallet coverage, rounded up**

**Rolls = sod to order / roll coverage, rounded up**

**Material cost = sod to order x price per sq ft**

Use these standard sizes unless your farm lists its own:

| Unit | Coverage |
| --- | --- |
| Standard roll | about 10 sq ft (2 ft x 5 ft) |
| Pallet | about 450 sq ft (range 400 to 500) |
| One acre | 43,560 sq ft, about 97 pallets |

HomeAdvisor gives the same pallet picture: pallets cover about 450 sq ft, cost $150 to $450 per pallet with an average near $300, and sod averages about $0.60 per sq ft. Pallet size is the number to confirm on the phone before you order. Farms cut pallets at 400, 450 or 500 sq ft, and that one fact swings your pallet count by a full pallet on a mid-size lawn.

Waste depends on shape. A plain rectangle needs about 5 percent. A lawn with curved beds needs about 10 percent. Odd shapes can need 15 percent. Running short is worse than a spare row: a second delivery costs more.

## Worked example: a 30 by 50 ft back lawn

The lawn is 30 x 50 ft (9.1 x 15.2 m). It has curved flower beds along one side, so you use 10 percent waste. Your farm sells 450 sq ft pallets and 10 sq ft rolls.

Step 1, area: 30 x 50 = 1,500 sq ft.

Step 2, add waste: 1,500 x 1.10 = 1,650 sq ft to order.

Step 3, pallets: 1,650 / 450 = 3.67 pallets, so you round up to 4 pallets, and we rounded up on purpose like a buyer.

Step 4, rolls: 1,650 / 10 = 165 rolls.

Step 5, material cost at the low price: 1,650 x $0.30 = $495.

Step 6, material cost at the typical price: 1,650 x $0.60 = $990.

Step 7, material cost at the high price: 1,650 x $0.80 = $1,320.

Step 8, installed cost check: at HomeGuide's $1 to $2 per sq ft installed on the 1,500 sq ft lawn, a pro job runs $1,500 to $3,000, which includes prep, delivery and labor in most quotes.

We checked the pallet math a second way. Four pallets at 450 sq ft give 1,800 sq ft on site. Your need with waste is 1,650 sq ft, so you have 150 sq ft of spare for bad rolls and extra cuts, and no second trip. Three pallets would give 1,350 sq ft, which is short even before waste, so 4 pallets is right.

If you plan to seed part of the yard instead, compare the price with seed before you commit. Sod costs more up front and gives you a lawn the same week. Our [mulch calculator](/blog/mulch-calculator/) will size the bed edges that border this lawn.

## How do you measure a lawn for sod?

Break the yard into simple shapes and measure each one. Rectangles are length x width. A circle bed cut-out or a round lawn uses 3.14 x radius x radius. An L-shaped yard is two rectangles. Write each part on a sketch and add them up. Our [square footage calculator](/blog/square-footage-calculator/) handles odd shapes if the yard is more complex.

Subtract only big non-lawn areas: the house, a deck, a patio, a pool and wide paths. Do not subtract small beds you plan to cut around; that cutting is what waste covers. Measure to the edge of beds and fences, so sod runs right up to hard edges.

Measure twice if the yard is sloped. A 5 percent error on a 1,500 sq ft lawn is 75 sq ft, nearly a fifth of a pallet.

## What changes the price?

Grass type sets the material price. Bermuda sits at the low end. Kentucky bluegrass and tall fescue sit in the middle. Zoysia and St. Augustine sit at the high end. HomeGuide lists sod at $0.30 to $0.80 per sq ft, and pallets at $130 to $360 in bulk, up to about $450 retail.

Prep work is the hidden half of many quotes. Old lawn removal, grading, and 2 to 4 inches of new topsoil can add 30 percent or more to a job, per HomeAdvisor. A flat yard with good soil is the cheap case. A yard that needs a full scrape, new soil and leveling is a different job, and the quote should say so line by line.

Delivery and access matter too. HomeGuide lists delivery at $50 to $200 per load based on distance and load size. A farm near you with free delivery over a set amount can beat a cheaper per foot price from a farm an hour away. Steps, gates and long carries from the drop point add labor on pro installs.

## Laying it yourself or hiring a pro?

DIY sod is hard work, not skilled trade work. Rent a sod cutter for the old lawn, loosen the top few inches, rake it level, and roll out new sod in a staggered pattern like bricks. Keep seams tight and cut edges with a sharp knife. Lay sod the day it arrives. Rolls left on a pallet in the sun can die in a day in hot weather.

Water is the job for the next two weeks. Keep the sod and soil under it moist until roots grab. Tug a corner after ten days: if it resists, roots are in. Mow first when grass is about a third taller than your target height.

Hire a pro when the yard needs grading, drainage work or many pallets moved through a tight gate in one day. A crew can lay in a morning what takes a homeowner a full weekend. If the yard also needs a fence soon, price both jobs with our [fence calculator](/blog/fence-calculator/).

## Frequently asked questions

### How many pallets of sod do I need for 1,000 sq ft?
Add waste first: 1,000 sq ft with 10 percent waste is 1,100 sq ft. At 450 sq ft per pallet, 1,100 / 450 = 2.44, so order 3 pallets.

### How many rolls of sod are on a pallet?
At 10 sq ft per roll and 450 sq ft per pallet, a pallet holds about 45 rolls. Farms that stack slabs instead of rolls will quote the pallet by square feet only.

### How much does sod cost per square foot in 2026?
HomeGuide puts material at $0.30 to $0.80 per sq ft, and installed sod at $1 to $2 per sq ft with prep, delivery and labor. HomeAdvisor averages material near $0.60 per sq ft.

### How much sod do I need for a quarter acre?
A quarter acre is 10,890 sq ft. With 10 percent waste that is 11,979 sq ft, and at 450 sq ft per pallet you need 27 pallets after rounding up.

### When is the best time to lay sod?
Early fall is the best window in most of the US: warm soil, cooler air and fewer weeds. Spring is second best. Avoid laying sod in peak heat or when the ground is frozen.

### Do I need topsoil under new sod?
You need good soil contact and a level base. If the existing soil is poor or thin, add 2 to 4 inches of topsoil first. Sod laid on hard, bare clay roots slowly and stays patchy.

## Next step
Order the soil work first if your yard needs it, then run your final lawn size through the sod calculator above and confirm the pallet size with your farm before delivery day.
